data.why: the repository ships a full BMKG/USGS earthquake catalog, fault/slab/region datasets, and sample CSVs (valid, missing-columns, mixed-invalid) made for the sidebar importer, so no synthetic data is needed.

goals: filter the national earthquake catalog by time window, magnitude, depth, province/kabupaten, and distance to faults or coastline to isolate an event set of interest
inspect hypocenters in 3D relative to the Slab2 subduction surface to read the Wadati-Benioff zone along a trench-perpendicular cross-section
review precomputed PSHA hazard maps (PGA and spectral acceleration by return period) and per-site hazard curves, and export the hazard grid as CSV
import a custom earthquake catalog (CSV/Excel) via the sidebar and check it against the app's validation (missing columns, invalid lat/lon/depth/date) before analysis
review filtered-catalog statistics and the event table, exporting the filtered events as CSV
compose a publication-ready A4-A2 map sheet (PNG/PDF) with legend, scale bar, north arrow, inset locator map, and data-source list, using a standard or spatial-planning (RTRW) template

review.summary: The tree follows E-QuakeVis's real stages (select events, map with tectonic layers, slab cross-section, PSHA review, stats/table export, import validation, publication map), and the screens I opened back up their nodes, with one exception (the slice-CSV screen). It needs fixing before filing: it leaves out several filters the README and plan name (time, depth, fault and volcano distance), the PSHA model-building purpose, the IM/return-period switch and a committed import, and the publication-map node still needs a confirmed replay.
